newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Exxon says Thai economy won't affect chemical plan.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says Thai economy won't affect chemical plan.

text.p: Exxon Corp is going ahead with a $450 million chemical investment in Thailand, despite the country's economic turmoil, a senior company official said on Friday.

"We have an attractive refinery (in Thailand) and we think we have the fundamentals to start work on the aromatics plant," said Ken Robertson, senior vice president, basic chemicals and intermediates of Exxon Chemical Co, a unit of Exxon Corp.
Robertson, speaking at a press conference, said the company was not concerned with the current economic turmoil in Thailand.
"We are looking at the long term. We were projecting they were going to be in a bad state," he said.
Robertson said the Exxon board would make a final decision on the project in September and he expected it to approve the building of the plant.

The Thai Board of Investment in May granted incentives for the 11.1 billion baht project to build a 350,000 tonne-per-year (tpa) paraxylene plant at Sri Racha where Exxon currently operates a 145,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery.
